ingest.note: Your bridge code receives raw telephony audio. You must decode and resample before sending to the model.

egress.note: Your bridge code must resample and encode model output back to telephony format.

potholes.note: With a custom FastAPI bridge, you are fully responsible for decoding, resampling, and encoding audio. No layer normalizes it for you.

No echo cancellation exists unless you add it. Your own TTS leaking back into the inbound path (carrier echo, speakerphone) false-triggers VAD and the agent interrupts itself in a loop. Gate VAD during agent speech or integrate an AEC.

A single uvicorn process with no drain is not production. Implement SIGTERM drain (finish calls, then exit), scale on concurrent calls, and set LB/proxy idle timeouts above max call duration or long calls die silently.

latency_evidence.methodology: Callsmith architecture-budget placeholder; benchmark in the deployment region before setting an SLO.

interruption.description: With a custom FastAPI bridge, you must manually implement interruption: detect user speech via VAD, cancel in-flight LLM/TTS requests, flush the outbound audio queue, and stop writing to the WebSocket.
interruption.code_hint: On VAD speech_start: (1) cancel LLM stream, (2) stop TTS, (3) outbound_queue.flush(), (4) stop sending to ws. No automatic handling — all manual.

deployment.self_host_notes: Self-host is the only path: there is no managed runtime for a custom bridge. You own process supervision, SIGTERM drain, concurrency scaling, warm pools (VAD session, provider connections), LB idle timeouts above max call duration, and frame-level diagnostics.

hosting_rules.reason: Custom FastAPI forces self-hosted ownership: your app owns the media WebSocket, codecs, resampling, cleanup, and incident debugging.
